title: v3.4.3 generates one ALB listener rule per hostname of an HTTPRoute/GRPCRoute — routes with several hostnames can exceed the ALB rules-per-listener quota

detection.reason: only a route with two or more hostnames on an LBC ALB Gateway gains listener rules, and the projection can neither count hostnames per route nor sum them per listener; the hint names the HTTPRoutes and GRPCRoutes whose Gateway class is the ALB controller's (a route on a Traefik or other Gateway is not the LBC's)

quote: [ALB Gateway Users] Double check your ALB rule limits, when using HTTP / GRPC route with multiple hostnames, a distinict rule per hostname is generated. Users who specify multiple hostnames per route will want to double check their ALB limits. https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/aws-load-balancer-controller/pull/4863/changes/2c657342ff09998a92fddf1fbcb945ecc7ef612a
remediation: Before upgrading, count rules × hostnames per ALB Gateway listener against the account's rules-per-listener quota (default 100); split routes or raise the quota where it is exceeded, otherwise the listener update is rejected and the route stays unprogrammed.
verifyCommand: kubectl get gatewayclasses,gateways,httproutes,grpcroutes -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items as $i | [$i[] | select(.kind == "GatewayClass" and .spec.controllerName == "gateway.k8s.aws/alb") | .metadata.name] as $c | [$i[] | select(.kind == "Gateway" and (.spec.gatewayClassName | IN($c[]))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name] as $g | $i[] | select(.kind == "HTTPRoute" or .kind == "GRPCRoute") | .metadata.namespace as $ns | select(any(.spec.parentRefs[]?; ((.namespace // $ns) + "/" + .name) | IN($g[]))) | select((.spec.hostnames // []) | length | . != 0 and . != 1) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) hostnames=\(.spec.hostnames | length) rules=\(.spec.rules | length) listener-rules=\((.spec.hostnames | length) * (.spec.rules | length))"'  # routes with several hostnames on an LBC ALB Gateway; the listener-rules column adds up per listener against the ALB quota

title: The LBC webhooks answer AdmissionReview v1 (admissionReviewVersions v1beta1 → v1) — the configurations were already admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1

detection.reason: the change is the admissionReviewVersions the webhook handlers accept, re-rendered by the chart on upgrade; nothing collected distinguishes it, the hint names the LBC webhooks (*.elbv2.k8s.aws, and vglobalaccelerator.aga.k8s.aws from 3.6) — not the VPC resource controller's *.vpc.k8s.aws

quote: Webhooks upgraded to v1: Admission webhooks were upgraded from v1beta1 to v1. Applied automatically on upgrade — no action needed (#4743)
remediation: No action: the chart has rendered admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1 configurations since 2.4.0, and 3.4 only moves admissionReviewVersions from v1beta1 to v1 (supported by every Kubernetes the controller runs on). Hand-maintained manifests pick the new value up with the 3.4 bundle.
verifyCommand: kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations,validatingwebhookconfigurations -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .webhooks[] | select(.name | test("\\.(elbv2|aga)\\.k8s\\.aws$")) | "\(.name) failurePolicy=\(.failurePolicy) namespaceSelector=\(.namespaceSelector // {} | tojson)"'  # the LBC admission webhooks installed on this cluster and the failure policy each runs with

title: v3.4.x repeats the vendor's apply-the-latest-CRDs note — no CRD schema changed between v3.3.0 and v3.4.3

detection.reason: nothing in the CRD files changed for this release (git diff v3.3.0..v3.4.3 over config/crd and helm crds is empty); the hint names the LBC CRDs

quote: Action : Please apply the latest CRD definitions
remediation: No CRD change ships in 3.4.x. Re-applying the CRDs is harmless; the 3.5 rules carry the next real schema change (gateway.k8s.aws v1 storage).
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd ingressclassparams.elbv2.k8s.aws -o json | jq -r '[.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] as $v | (.spec.versions[] | select(.storage) | .schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec.properties // {} | keys) as $k | "served=\($v | join(",")) spec fields=\($k | join(","))"'  # the installed CRD schema; nothing new absent from the field list means the CRDs were not re-applied for this release
